articles.title: CX Chrome Void
articles.summary: Semi-matte near-black base with glossy chrome patches and bright sparkle flecks. Reads as a blacked-out car with faint grey smudges, like dark gunmetal or a matte wrap with a few polished spots; no sharp shapes survive.
articles.what: Pure mirror chrome ↔ absolute matte black. Maximum possible material contrast. Up close: Near-black charcoal ground with fine slanted hairline grain and a loose scatter of soft squarish grey-lilac patches from pinhead to thumbnail size. The patches are the spots where the spec turns chrome; in the paint picture they are only slightly lighter than the black. Colour is a fixed black. From a distance: Reads as a blacked-out car with faint grey smudges, like dark gunmetal or a matte wrap with a few polished spots; no sharp shapes survive. Measured spec (average): metal 73, roughness 172, coat 120. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put CX Chrome Void on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: large areas show the chrome patches
Trim and bumpers: dark stealth look
Dark numbers vanish; use white, silver or bright colour numbers with an outline.
White, chrome or red numbers and wide stripes: strong contrast on the dark base
Pairs well with: chrome, white, red, silver.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not full chrome: metal averages only 73, most of the surface is dark and dull
Not matte black wrap: the chrome patches flash in sun
Avoid: glossy patches fight busy decals, all-black hides body lines in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 73 (pearl-level metal), roughness 172 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 120 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: glossy patches fight busy decals, all-black hides body lines in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: white, chrome or red numbers and wide stripes: strong contrast on the dark base; fine lightning or geometric lines in a bright colour: pop clearly on the void
Patterns to avoid: dark or subtle patterns: vanish on the black; fine glitter or dot patterns: compete with the chrome patches
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat panels: ghost graphics on the dark base; brushed streaks: adds directional chrome contrast on the metal patches
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
